findings: Fit with decisions: the rule, wording and compliance test live in one module, anvil/attribution.py, read by scaffold, onboard and the checks gate. This gives one source of truth for the default line. Dependencies point one way: gates, scaffold and onboard import attribution, and attribution imports nothing from them.

Decision 0012 is recorded in the format of the existing records (Context, Decision, Consequences). It states the trade-offs honestly: a deterministic bespoke-credit pattern can false-fail, only the index page is checked, and cloudflare-worker is marked ships_pages false. No accepted decision is broken.

Gate integration is small and fail-closed. check_attribution returns None when there is no HTML deliverable, so non-web projects are unaffected. Output is added only when the check applies, and a recorded owner exception is honoured. The exception form is strict (exact line shape), so a loose note cannot weaken the gate.

Scaffold and onboard follow existing structure. The new blueprint flag ships_pages is a small data-driven switch, not hard-coded blueprint names. Onboard writes only into ONBOARDING.md and never overwrites existing project files.

Minor, non-blocking: the ships_pages flag is read with blueprint.get and only the first spec gets the requirement. This is acceptable for the current two blueprints. A later blueprint with several page specs would need the flag documented.

Minor, non-blocking: the full suite shows 5 failures in test_autonomous_line and test_governed_delivery. They come from GITHUB_ACTOR in the runner and fail the same way on an unmodified checkout. I re-ran the suite and saw the same 5 failures. The builder report discloses this. It is an environment issue outside the authorised surface and not an architecture defect. The operator must decide how the gate handles it.
The earlier loopback reason (missing builder report and literals) is resolved: runs/wo-gh-43/builder.output.md now exists.
